items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: before that, I used to listen to Harry James as a great player and everything, but when the bebop thing came out, it changed my whole life

ctx.x: With me, I never thought of it as an art form or that, I just heard it and I said well this is what I want to do. And I thought if I got good enough at this, you know, I could possibly

make a living doing it, which was a big mistake you know. Even like the Charlie Parkers couldn’t make a living, who was, to me, one of the best or the best jazz player around ever. But I dug it. I mean there was some vital — something vital about it. It tells the whole story about life and I mean I just fell in love with it. And before that, I used to listen to Harry James as a great player and everything, but when the bebop thing came out, it changed my whole life you know? And I keep telling all these guys,…
The timing was a little off then.
